generated_by: Proposed under data/pair.md, confirmed by hand.
note: One problem, two or more attempts at it. Every line is two clauses — the shared problem, then how each party answers it. The tier records how far apart the answers are: same is the same thing twice, similar is the same lever at a different volume or scope, different is a different kind of answer rather than more or less of one. Degree is similar; kind is different.

pairs.label: KiwiSaver
pairs.problem: How do we get people saving for retirement?
pairs.line: National and NZ First both want KiwiSaver made compulsory. Same policy, a month apart.
pairs.confidence_note: Scored as a deliberate like-for-like. Same size, same rungs on all four axes.

pairs.label: Solar
pairs.problem: How do we get solar panels onto roofs?
pairs.line: Labour, National and the Greens all want to help pay for your solar panels. Three subsidies, one idea.
pairs.confidence_note: National's record is the thin one — a $7m fund with no published detail beyond the headline.

pairs.label: Marine
pairs.problem: How do we protect the ocean?
pairs.line: The Greens and TOP both want 30% of the ocean protected and bottom trawling gone. Same target, same year.
pairs.confidence_note: Size mismatch. Same target, same instrument, different rungs — a question for Sort, raised by Pair.

pairs.label: Supermarkets
pairs.line: NZ First and TOP both want the supermarkets broken up. NZ First would legislate it. TOP would let the Commerce Commission do it.
pairs.confidence_note: Size mismatch. TOP's sits inside a wider innovation package, which is why it reads larger.

pairs.label: Doctors
pairs.problem: How do we make seeing a GP affordable?
pairs.line: Labour and Te Pāti Māori both want the cost taken out of seeing a GP. Labour for everyone, TPM for whānau under $60,000.
pairs.confidence_note: Size mismatch, and it may be the right call — one is universal, the other a cohort.

pairs.label: Transport
pairs.problem: How do we make getting around cheaper?
pairs.line: Labour and TOP both want cheaper public transport. Labour would cap it. TOP would make it free.
pairs.confidence_note: TOP's sits inside a 30-year infrastructure framework, which is why it lands so much later.

pairs.label: Asset taxes
pairs.line: Four parties want new taxes on assets. Four different ways to do it.
pairs.confidence_note: Size mismatch across four records. The shared premise is inferred from the instruments, not stated by any party.

pairs.label: Emissions
pairs.problem: What do we do about farm emissions?
pairs.line: ACT and TOP both have a plan for farm emissions. ACT would keep them out of the trading scheme. TOP would bring them in.
pairs.confidence_note: Both records thin on timing. The opposition itself is explicit in both descriptions.

pairs.label: Gentailers
pairs.problem: How do we keep the lights on in a dry year?
pairs.line: Three parties want the dry-year problem fixed. The Greens would build a public generator, NZ First would split the existing ones, TOP would leave them alone and pay for backup.
pairs.confidence_note: Size mismatch across the three. TOP's page rejects NZ First's structural separation by name.

pairs.label: Teachers
pairs.problem: How do we keep good teachers?
pairs.line: ACT and TOP both want more pay for teachers. ACT would pay the best ones more. TOP would pay them all properly.
pairs.confidence_note: Different sectors — ACT's is schools, TOP's is early childhood. The shared problem is retention, not the workforce.

pairs.label: Voting
pairs.line: NZ First would take the vote off permanent residents. Te Pāti Māori would give it back to prisoners.
pairs.confidence_note: Te Pāti Māori's record is broader than the pair — it covers rehabilitation, the Steps to Freedom payment and minimum entitlements as well as voting. Published on the basis that voting is named in its title and is the element the pair turns on. Splitting the franchise element into its own record would tighten it.
